title: TS Streaming Adapter: Contraction & Expansion Patterns for Dual-Consumer Runtime Interop
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem summary: We need a robust TypeScript SDK surface that lets teams consume the same inference stream using two different runtime patterns: standard async iterator-based consumers (server/node legacy code) and browser ReadableStream-style consumers (fetch/streams APIs). Current attempts either duplicate buffering logic or expose awkward adapters that leak implementation details.

Goal: Provide a small, well-documented adapter layer in the TS SDK that supports two complementary patterns: 
- Contraction: reduce emission frequency (coalesce tokens/frames) to make async-iterator consumers efficient for high-throughput low-latency usage.
- Expansion: transform batched/compact frames into fine-grained events for ReadableStream consumers expecting small chunks.

Constraints and non-goals: 
- Not a full protocol redesign — must work with existing streaming protocol used by Redwood inference runtime.
- Avoid runtime dependencies (no heavy polyfills). Aim for a light-weight adapter that composes with existing SDK helper primitives.
- Do not change server-side streaming semantics; adapters are client-side only.

Key behaviors: 
- Backpressure-aware bridging: adapter respects async iterator pull indications and ReadableStream desiredSize semantics where available.
- Deterministic cancellation: propagate cancellation from both consumer types to server with a single code path; avoid double-close races.
- Checkpoint/resume: emit periodic checkpoints (idempotent tokens) so resumable consumers can resume after transient network failures.
- Single source of truth: adapter should allow a single read loop that fans out transformed frames to both consumer styles without duplicating the network stream consumption.

Deliverables: 
- Implement adapter in ts-sdk/core/streaming with tests + benchmarks.
- Examples: two example apps (node worker using for-await, browser demo using ReadableStream + pipeTo).
- Docs: migration guide and recipe for wrapping custom transformation logic.

Performance targets: 
- CPU overhead of adapter < 5% for typical generation workloads.
- Added median latency < 2ms at 1k tokens/sec compared to raw stream consumption.

Success criteria: 
- Internal e2e tests showing both consumer types read the same token sequence without loss or duplication across reconnects.
- Good ergonomics validated by two partner teams (Console telemetry ingestion, Samples repo).
acceptance_criteria: Adapter exposes a minimal API: createAdapter(streamTransport, options) -> { asyncIterator(), readableStream() }
Cancellation from asyncIterator.throw() and ReadableStream.cancel() both shut down transport exactly once
Checkpoints are emitted every N tokens (configurable) and used by resume tests
Docs include migration recipe and 2 runnable examples (node + browser)
Benchmarks attached and show CPU <5% overhead compared to baseline
comments: 2026-02-28 - Triage: Initial write-up and scoping. Decided to prioritize a single adapter module instead of two separate adapters to reduce maintenance overhead.

2026-03-03 - Architecture meeting notes: Chose contraction via token-coalescing window (configurable maxTokens and maxMs) and expansion via framed-splitting using a lightweight framing codec. Agreed to avoid streaming transforms that allocate large intermediate buffers.
2026-03-05 - Design feedback (PM - Jordan Lee): Emphasize checkpoints for Dedicated customers who may experience preemption; added checkpoint configuration and resume API to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-07 - Engineering review (Rina Okafor): Raised concern about Node stream desiredSize mapping; decided to emulate desiredSize heuristics for async iterator consumers by tracking pending consumer Promises and adjusting contraction window size.
2026-03-09 - PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/1429 - initial adapter implementation + unit tests

2026-03-11 - QA: Ran flaky reconnect test 50x against local test harness. Found a race where cancel + immediate reconnect could cause duplicate resume tokens. Added de-duplication check and test coverage.
2026-03-12 - Next: add README examples, record microbenchmarks, and schedule API review with Docs and Samples teams.
implementation_notes: Keep the public API tiny. Implementation will use a single consumption loop that reads transport frames and routes them through small synchronous transforms into two internal FIFOs: one optimized for coalesced async iterator yields, one for small-chunk ReadableStream pushes. Use SharedArrayBuffer-free queues to keep browser compatibility. Expose knobs: maxTokens, maxMs, checkpointInterval, expansionFrameSize.
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for cancellation and checkpointing. 2) Integration test with local runtime to simulate reconnect and resume. 3) Browser smoke test (Chrome + Firefox) that pipes readableStream to a TransformStream and ensures ordering. 4) Load test generating 2k tokens/sec for 10min, verify <5% CPU overhead.
risks_and_mitigations: risk: backpressure mismatches causing memory growth - mitigation: enforce bounded internal FIFO with backpressure signaling to transport (stall reads)
risk: double-close races when both consumers cancel - mitigation: single shutdown coordinator with idempotent close
risk: browser compatibility for small frame timing - mitigation: polyfill tests and examples that degrade gracefully
notes_for_code_review: Pay attention to shutdown choreography in adapter.test.ts, look for potential unhandled rejection windows. Ensure examples do not rely on global fetch stream behaviors only available in Chromium. Prefer explicit hooks in the README for embedding in frameworks (Next.js, Deno).
